scenes.heading: Solving quadratic equations
scenes.say: When does a thrown ball land? How wide must a garden be to have an area of sixty square metres? Both questions lead to quadratic equations. In this video you'll learn how to solve them.
scenes.caption: When does a thrown ball land? How wide must a garden be to have an area of 60 m²? Both questions lead to quadratic equations. In this video you'll learn how to solve them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A lamp wired through two switches is off, so at least one switch is off
scenes.science: If A × B = 0, then A = 0 or B = 0
scenes.breaks: It only works for zero. If two numbers multiply to 6, you can't say anything about either one.
scenes.say: Picture a lamp wired through two switches, one after the other. If the lamp is off, at least one switch must be off, so you check each one. The null factor law is the same: if two factors multiply to zero, at least one is zero, so you set each factor equal to zero.

scenes.heading: The method
scenes.say: Here's the method. First, rearrange so one side is zero. Then factorise fully. Set each factor equal to zero and solve. Finally, check your answers in the original equation. And never divide by x, or you'll lose the solution x equals zero.

scenes.heading: Solutions are x-intercepts
notes: Where the curve meets the x-axis
scenes.say: Here are the axes, and now the graph of y equals x squared minus x minus six. Watch where it crosses the x-axis: at negative two and at three. Those are exactly the solutions of x squared minus x minus six equals zero, because on the x-axis, y is zero.
scenes.caption: Here is the graph of y = x² − x − 6. It crosses the x-axis at −2 and 3. Those are the solutions of x² − x − 6 = 0, because on the x-axis, y = 0.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Solve 2x² − 5x = 3.
scenes.say: Solve two x squared minus five x equals three. First make one side zero by subtracting three. Factorise to get x minus three, times two x plus one. Set each factor to zero. So x equals three, or x equals negative one half.
scenes.caption: Solve 2x² − 5x = 3. Make one side zero: 2x² − 5x − 3 = 0. Factorise: (x − 3)(2x + 1) = 0. So x = 3 or x = −1/2.

scenes.heading: When it won't factorise
scenes.question: Solve x² + 6x + 2 = 0 exactly.
scenes.say: This one doesn't factorise with whole numbers, so complete the square: x plus three, all squared, minus seven equals zero. Add seven to both sides. Take the square root, and remember plus or minus. So x equals negative three plus or minus root seven.
scenes.caption: This doesn't factorise with whole numbers, so complete the square: (x + 3)² − 7 = 0. Add 7, then take the square root with ±: x = −3 ± √7.

points: Factorise, then set each factor to 0
Reject answers that make no sense
scenes.say: Quick recap. Make one side zero, factorise, and set each factor to zero. Never divide by x. When you take a square root, use plus or minus. And in worded problems, reject answers that make no sense, like a negative length. Now try the practice questions!
